Emma Chen: hey folks — Emma here, just joined the payments squad. I'm trying to switch to the payments service account to test RBAC but `kubectl config get-contexts` only shows my user context. I tried `kubectl config use-context payments` and it says context not found. What is the recommended quick flow to get a kubeconfig / context for a SA? :wave:

Raj Patel: welcome! short answer: service accounts don't show up as contexts automatically. You either generate a kubeconfig for the SA (token + ca) or impersonate. Which cloud / auth flow are you on? EKS, GKE, or self-hosted?

Emma Chen: EKS (IRSA). I'm using aws-sso to authenticate locally and don't have any SA tokens.

Samir Khan (eng-infra): easiest path is infra creating a short-lived kubeconfig for the SA and putting it in the team vault. Alternatively, if your user has impersonation rights you can `--as` the SA. Which do you prefer?

Raj Patel: here are quick steps if infra wants you to generate locally (note differences by k8s version):
```bash
# <1.24: secret-based token flow
kubectl -n payments get serviceaccount app-tester -o jsonpath='{.secrets[0].name}'
kubectl -n payments get secret <secret-name> -o go-template='{{.data.token | base64decode}}' > /tmp/sa.token
kubectl config set-credentials payments-app-sa --token="$(cat /tmp/sa.token)"
kubectl config set-context payments-sa --cluster=aws-cluster --user=payments-app-sa --namespace=payments
kubectl config use-context payments-sa

# >=1.24: token subcommand
kubectl -n payments create token app-tester > /tmp/sa.token
```
If you don't have permission to `get secret` then infra will need to create it for you.

Emma Chen: I can't run `get secret` — permission denied. Could you create a kubeconfig and share it? Also worried about storing tokens in plain-text.

Cassie Lee (security): do not upload raw tokens to public channels. If infra issues a kubeconfig, make it short lived (24h) and store it in the team vault with limited access. Also rotate after use. @Samir can infra put the kubeconfig in the payments Vault entry?

Samir Khan: yes — I'll create a 24h kubeconfig for `app-tester` and add it to the payments vault entry, then DM the link to you. I can also create a RoleBinding for the two namespaces you mentioned if needed. @Emma, confirm which namespaces you need access to.

Emma Chen: payments and payments-staging please. Thanks!

DevEx Bot: reminder: for future onboardings see internal doc /docs/onboarding/kubernetes-quickstart and run `kubectl auth can-i` to validate permissions quickly.

Raj Patel: alternative (no token): impersonation example — requires infra to grant `impersonate` on serviceaccounts:
`kubectl --as=system:serviceaccount:payments:app-tester auth can-i get pods -n payments`
This avoids creating a persistent token but needs impersonate permission.

Emma Chen: perfect — I'll wait for the vault link. appreciate the quick help! :pray:
